description: Performance budgets for bundle size enforcement. Caps are set from the 2026-09-26 measured build (post PurgeCSS rewrite, locale chunk split, assetsInlineLimit: 0) plus ~7-10% headroom. Revised 2026-09-30 after WU-1 (react-router 8.4.0) and again after WU-2 (RTK 2.13 + react-redux 9, total only): fresh measured builds with human approval (PR #146 / stacked WU-2 PR).

default.description: Default chunk size limit (97kb raw, 30kb gzip). Measured: i18n 54652 raw / 18278 gzip.

vendor.description: Vendor chunk limit (288kb raw, 97kb gzip). Measured WU-2 (2026-09-30): vendor 289067 raw (react-redux landed here); WU-1 was 287121 raw / 91660 gzip (react-router 8.4.0; baseline dev 195288 raw / 62130 gzip).

main.description: Main chunk limit (195kb raw, 72kb gzip). Raised 160000→200000 with human approval (About CRUD WU-4, 2026-10-04): react-hook-form now rides the lazy /admin/about chunk, main measured 190071 raw (zod stays in main for sync hydration).

total.description: Total JS bundle size limit (912kb raw, 278kb gzip). Raised 912176 -> 933888 (912 KiB) for the About-only backend cutover branch (feat/navbar-avatar-settings-session, auto-mode per owner directive 2026-10-28): measured CI/local 904.8 KiB vs dev baseline 883.1 KiB (+21.7 KiB of real feature code — navbar avatar/session restore/preferences, contact inbox page+route, About API sync (apiSlice/contentSync), backend image-upload seam). No new libraries; main 92.5 KiB and vendor 290.0 KiB stay under their own caps, headroom 7.4 KiB. Previous: raised 861184 -> 896256 (896 KiB) for the admin-about-table AMEND (WU-10..15, measured 875551 raw = 855 KiB, +20.7 KiB headroom) — owner-approved 2026-10-20; all other caps untouched, gzip headroom vast. Previous: raised 860160 -> 861184 (841 KiB) for the admin-about-table epic (vitrina + per-field modal, measured 860537 raw, +377 B over the old cap) — owner-approved 2026-10-20; all other caps untouched, gzip headroom vast. Raised 802816 -> 860160 and gzip 266240 -> 284672 (rtk-query-stub epic, auto-mode per SPEC R-7, 2026-10-17): the RTK Query apiSlice stub (createApi core subpath + reducer + middleware in the root store, plan rev.3 §3.7) grows main to 133773 raw and the measured total to 839696 raw / 272851 gzip; vendor 290707 untouched, RHF still rides lazy admin chunks. History: 786432 -> 802816 (raw only; gzip unchanged) under the technologies-crud epic auto-mode (#258 / PR #259, 2026-10-16): the new lazy /admin/technologies chunk (AdminTechnologiesPage 7383 raw + 570 css) grew the measured total to 775.2 KiB vs the 768 KiB cap — main 99159 and vendor 290707 untouched, resume-lazy-rhf-chunk intact (RHF rides the new chunk). History: 761856 -> 786432 (raw only; gzip 238737 << 266240) under the job-field-edit epic auto-mode (2026-10-14): FieldEditForm + shared field zod slices grew the lazy /admin/jobs chunk, measured 766393 raw (748.4 KiB) vs merge-base dev 742.9 KiB (+5.5 KiB, all in AdminJobsPage chunk — main 97434 and vendor 290707 untouched, resume-lazy-rhf-chunk intact). Headroom kept for future lazy admin chunks. History: 737280/258048 -> 761856/266240 with human approval (project-images WU-5 / PR #207, 2026-10-10: FileUpload kit +8.6 KiB). Earlier: 655360/225280 -> 737280/258048 (Skills CRUD WU-5, 2026-10-06, measured 685467); Projects CRUD 625000->655360 (2026-10-06); About CRUD WU-4 510000->625000 (2026-10-04); WU-2 485000->510000 (2026-09-30).

assets.description: Non-JS assets budget, REBASED by issue #298 (2026-10-18). Semantics changed: check-bundle walk() now counts EVERY binary asset in public/ (webp/svg/png, excluding index.html entry shell and stats.html report) and caps their SUM against this value — the category was never measured before. Measured after the top-8 image recompression (webp q75, <=1600px): 4,805,096 B before -> 423,651 B after (56 files); cap set to 445000 = sum + ~5% headroom. History: was 122880 as an INDIVIDUAL non-JS file limit (measured: index CSS 120694, sdd-134-css post C1-C5); the per-file CSS check still runs against this cap and index CSS 120694 remains well under 445000.
